message.content:
Based on my search, here's a comprehensive guide to understanding pregnancy test results:

## Types of Pregnancy Tests

**Urine Tests (Home Tests):**
- Available at drugstores, pharmacies, and grocery stores
- About 99% accurate when used correctly
- Results appear within 2-10 minutes
- Can be strip tests, midstream tests, or digital tests

**Blood Tests (Medical):**
- Done at a doctor's office or hospital
- More sensitive than urine tests
- Can detect pregnancy 7-10 days after conception
- Measures exact hCG levels
- Results take a few hours to two days

## How to Read Results

### **Positive Result**
- **Single window test:** Two lines appear (control line + test line)
- **Two-window test:** Line in control window AND plus sign (+) or line in second window
- **Digital test:** Displays "Pregnant," "Yes," or a smiley face
- **Important:** Any visible colored line in the test region, no matter how faint, is considered positive

### **Negative Result**
- **Single window test:** Only one line (control line)
- **Two-window test:** Line in control window, empty second window or minus (-) symbol
- **Digital test:** Displays "Not Pregnant" or "No"

### **Invalid Result**
- No lines appear at all, OR
- Control line doesn't appear (even if test line is visible)
- Means the test didn't work properly—repeat with a new test

## When to Test for Best Accuracy

| Timing | Accuracy |
|--------|----------|
| 7-10 days after ovulation | Very low—testing is usually too early |
| 11-14 days after ovulation (before missed period) | Variable (50-90% depending on test sensitivity) |
| **Day of missed period** | **High (97-99%)** |
| **1 week after missed period** | **Very high (over 99%)** |

## Tips for Accurate Results

1. **Use first morning urine**—most concentrated hCG levels
2. **Don't overhydrate** before testing—dilutes hCG
3. **Check expiration date** on the test
4. **Follow instructions exactly**
5. **Read results within the time window** (usually 3-10 minutes)
6. **Use a midstream urine sample**

## Understanding Faint Lines

A **faint but colored line** appearing within the reading window usually means:
- You're in very early pregnancy
- hCG levels are still building up
- This is still a **positive result**

## Evaporation Lines vs. True Positives

| Evaporation Line | True Positive |
|-----------------|---------------|
| Appears AFTER the time limit (10+ minutes) | Appears WITHIN the time limit (2-10 minutes) |
| Usually colorless, gray, or very faint | Has color (pink or blue) |
| Caused by urine drying on the test | Caused by hCG detection |

## What Can Affect Results

**False Negatives (test says negative, but you're pregnant):**
- Testing too early
- Diluted urine
- Expired test
- Not following instructions
- Certain medications (diuretics, antihistamines)

**False Positives (test says positive, but you're not pregnant):**
- Reading test after time limit
- Certain fertility medications containing hCG
- Recent miscarriage or pregnancy
- Some medical conditions (rare)
- Chemical pregnancy

## When to See a Doctor

- If you get a positive result—schedule a prenatal appointment
- If you get conflicting results on multiple tests
- If you continue testing negative but miss multiple periods
- If you have symptoms of pregnancy but negative tests
- If you've been trying to conceive for 12+ months (6+ months if over 35)

Sources:

2. https://www.parents.com/pregnancy-test-delayed-second-line-8594630
3. https://www.webmd.com/baby/pregnancy-tests
4. https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diagnostics/9703-pregnancy-tests
5. https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/getting-pregnant/in-depth/home-pregnancy-tests/art-20047940
6. https://www.babylist.com/hello-baby/how-to-read-a-pregnancy-test

8. https://mommed.com/blogs/breastfeeding-pregnancy/pregnancy-test-strips-results-a-comprehensive-guide-to-interpretation-and-accuracy?srsltid=AfmBOoqOFgDVOgug3DRLBIlMkIg8EMHky2F8a1IJI_78zmutmEl9keeS
